deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up exterior powers of bounded operators between Hilbert spaces, as preparation for his Fredholm-determinant and nuclear-operator work (cf. Produits tensoriels topologiques, 1955; 'La théorie de Fredholm', Bull. SMF 1956). On the previous page he defined, for u_1,...,u_n in L(E,F), the operator u_1∧...∧u_n = φ_n∘(u_1⊗...⊗u_n)∘a_n. Here a_n is the antisymmetrising injection of Λ^n E into ⊗^n E and φ_n is the quotient map onto Λ^n F. He showed ||u_1∧...∧u_n|| ≤ Π||u_i||, so the operator extends to the Hilbert completions Λ̂^n E → Λ̂^n F. On this page he records the functorial rules, writing Λ̄u for the n-th exterior power of a single u.

(10) Functoriality: Λ̄(v∘u) = Λ̄v∘Λ̄u.

(11) Adjoints: (u_1∧...∧u_n)* = u_1*∧...∧u_n*, and in particular (Λ̄u)* = Λ̄(u*).
- The mixed form is reduced to the single-operator form by polarization. One writes u_1∧...∧u_n as (1/n!) times a signed sum, over subsets {i_1<...<i_p} of {1..n}, of Λ̄(u_{i_1}+...+u_{i_p}).
- The single-operator case is checked on decomposable vectors using the Gram-determinant identity for the inner product on Λ^n: (Λ̄u a_1∧...∧a_n, b_1∧...∧b_n) = det((u a_i, b_j)) = det((a_i, u* b_j)) = (a_1∧...∧a_n, Λ̄u* b_1∧...∧b_n).

Consequence for E=F: u ↦ Λ̄^n u from L(E) to L(Λ̄^n E) is multiplicative, *-preserving, and sends hermitian operators to hermitian ones and positive operators to positive ones. The positivity argument: if h = k² with k ≥ 0, then Λ̄h = (Λ̄k)² with Λ̄k hermitian.

(12) Commutation with real powers: (Λ̄^n h)^α = Λ̄^n(h^α) for h ≥ 0 and α > 0. The argument runs over the end of this page and the next:
- For integer α it follows from (10).
- For α = 1/m it follows from uniqueness of positive m-th roots.
- For rational α it follows by combining the two.
- For real α it follows by norm-continuity of α ↦ H^α, together with continuity of u ↦ Λ̄u.

Purpose: this is a step toward Proposition 1 (next page), which presumably feeds polar decomposition, |Λu| = Λ|u|, and hence the singular-value / s-number estimates. These are Weyl–Horn type inequalities, used in Grothendieck's Fredholm theory for nuclear operators and in the bounds on Fredholm determinant coefficients.
errors: Polarization sign: the standard identity is n!·u_1∧...∧u_n = Σ_{S⊆{1..n}} (-1)^{n-|S|} Λ̄(Σ_{i∈S} u_i). The transcription has (-1)^p; this is correct only up to the global sign (-1)^n, or else it is a misreading of (-1)^{n-p}.

Normalisation: whether u∧...∧u (n times) equals Λ̄^n u or n!·Λ̄^n u depends on the convention for a_n and φ_n. The factor 1/n! in the polarization formula must match that convention; the page does not make this explicit.
Minor slip: after 'supposons E = F' the map is still written as going from L(E,F) to L(Λ̄^n E, Λ̄^n F).
On the next page the formula proved here as (12) is referred to as (11): a numbering inconsistency.
The step 'Λ̄k is hermitian' tacitly uses (11) applied to a hermitian k. This is fine, but it is the reason (11) had to come first.

ideas.what: Bounded extension of u_1∧...∧u_n to Hilbert-space exterior powers, with norm ≤ Π||u_i||
ideas.modern_name: Exterior powers of bounded operators on Hilbert space (second-quantization / fermionic Fock-space functor)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weyl, Horn; Segal for Fock space)
ideas.where_published: La théorie de Fredholm (Bull. SMF 1956) and Produits tensoriels topologiques use exterior powers in this way

ideas.what: Functoriality and *-compatibility of Λ^n via the Gram-determinant inner product
ideas.modern_name: Λ^n is a *-functor; ⟨Λu a, b⟩ = det⟨u a_i, b_j⟩

ideas.what: Polarization expressing mixed wedge products through Λ^n of partial sums
ideas.modern_name: Polarization identity for symmetric multilinear maps

ideas.what: Λ^n preserves positivity and commutes with real powers h^α
ideas.modern_name: Λ^n commutes with continuous functional calculus of positive operators, giving |Λ^n u| = Λ^n|u|
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (used in proofs of Weyl's inequalities, Horn 1950)

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but entirely standard verifications of the functorial properties of exterior powers of Hilbert-space operators. They prepare the Fredholm/s-number theory that Grothendieck published in 1955–56. Nothing here is new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: The sign in the polarization sum should probably be read as (-1)^{n-p}; the image is hard to read at that point.
Formula (11) is first written and struck out as (Λ̄u)*=Λ̄u*. It is then rewritten as a brace containing two lines: (u_1∧...∧u_n)* = u_1*∧...∧u_n* and (Λ̄u)* = Λ̄(u*).
The text 'transforme des hermitiens en hermitiens' is an interlinear insertion above the struck-out word 'commute avec l'involution'.
